title: Context Optimization: Comprehensive Lazy-Loading Architecture
description:
Implement systematic lazy-loading across WAI to minimize token usage and maximize efficiency.

**Goal:** Reduce unnecessary file loading by 80%+ through intelligent load policies, reference folder organization, and on-demand file access patterns.

**Success Criteria:**
1. ✅ Session briefing shows file loading stats (DONE)
2. ✅ Hook optimized to avoid redundant reads (DONE)
3. ✅ Conditional token usage display (DONE)
4. ✅ Load policy metadata added to WAI-File-Index.json schema
5. ✅ Reference folder restructured with README explaining load policies
6. ✅ Guide updated with lazy-loading philosophy and patterns
7. ✅ All WAI-Spoke files categorized: always/summary_only/on_request/never

**Scope:**
- File index schema enhancement (load_policy field)
- Reference folder organization and documentation
- Session log optimization (only load on closeout)
- Lugs file optimization (summary stats vs full load)
- Deprecated/archived file blocking
- Agent guidance for on-demand loading

**Out of Scope:**
- Changes to core WAI-Guide.md structure (only add lazy-loading section)
- Breaking changes to existing file locations
- Hub-side changes (spoke-only optimization)

**Constraints:**
- Must preserve backward compatibility with existing spokes
- Must not require manual migration steps
- Performance: briefing generation must stay under 500ms
- Zero breaking changes to wai CLI commands

**Estimated Impact:**
- Token savings: 100K+ per session (50% of budget freed)
- Briefing clarity: Agents understand what's loaded vs available
- Developer experience: Faster session starts, clearer context
- Scalability: Efficiency improves as WAI-Spoke grows
resolution_reason: All 7 success criteria completed: (1-3) Session briefing, hook optimization, token display, (4-7) File index schema, reference folder reorg, guide update, file categorization. WAI-File-Index.json created with load policies, reference/README.md explains lazy-loading, WAI-Guide.md updated with philosophy section.
